newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Li Yun-chung, the fugitive drug suspect, is in Rangoon with the knowledge of the Burmese junta and is unlikely to be returned to Thailand, a source says. A contract to kill Li is understood to have been issued by the people who helped him escape, to shut him up should he return to Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)

- In a dramatic about-face, police have resumed their investigation into alleged electoral fraud involving Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and other government politicians, one day after it had been announced the charges were being dropped. Police chief Pracha Promnok announces that police investigators have been instructed to continue searching for evidence and that the cases will proceed accordingly if more evidence was found. (THE NATION)

- Since it appears that the government wants to delay and play up the Tha Chana forest scandal case against the party to overshadow the administration's own mistakes, the Democrats have its MP Suthep Thaugsuban surrender to face malfeasance and forest encroachment charges. Police initially demand Suthep turn himself in this Friday, although the Interior Ministry has approved a police request last Friday to arrest him. (THE NATION)

- Eight business groups have received a financial boost following the approval of 28 new licences both for life and non-life insurance businesses. The Cabinet has approved the Commerce Ministry's proposal for granting 12 new life insurance licences and 16 new non-life insurance licences. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand's (EGAT) State Enterprise Employees Association has issued its first two open letters to the public reaffirming its opposition to the power utility's planned privatisation programme. The EGAT union cites the final privatisation study made by EGAT's advisers as saying power tariffs would have to be increased as a result of the listing of the agency's power plants. (THE NATION)
